newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Boeing has made no new EU offer on McDonnell deal.
newsitem.headline: Boeing has made no new EU offer on McDonnell deal.

text.p: Boeing Co has made no new offer since Tuesday afternoon to win European Union approval for its merger with McDonnell Douglas, increasing the chances that the deal could be banned in Europe.
"We have not put in any new offer," Boeing's vice-president for European affairs Jim Frank told Reuters.

Frank was speaking as the EU's advisory committee on concentrations met to discuss the $14 billion merger. It followed a warning by the European Commission on Tuesday that it would prohibit the deal unless Boeing made serious concessions.

Brussels-based lawyers, who have been closely watching the fight between the U.S. aircraft giant and the EU, have been speculating that Boeing would improve its offer to avoid the deal being killed altogether. "Nobody completely believes it will be blocked," one said.
National antitrust experts sitting on the EU's advisory committee recommended on July 4 that the merger should not be allowed in its current form.

The Commission is expected to give its final ruling on July 23, but left little doubt on Tuesday about its determination to play tough on Boeing by throwing its support behind its competition chief Karel Van Miert -- in what was seen as a repeat performance of next week's meeting.
